findings.title: Shared confidence and numeric checks are written once
findings.description: `check_confidence` is one vectorized check. Label series and signal sequences both call it, so the range rule lives in one place. `as_integer`, `as_real` and `require_real` in `value_checks.py` are the only coercion path. Declarations, `ConfidenceRange` and `SignalEvent` all use them. `labels.py` and `signals.py` have no element loops. Tests enforce this by AST scan.

findings.title: Declarations validate eagerly and bind with full issue reporting
findings.description:
`bind_parameters` collects every issue in declared order, followed by the unknown names sorted. It rejects bools, fractional integers, NaN and infinity. It returns a read-only mapping. Omitted and explicit-default values bind to equal results, and the test asserts the canonical bytes match.

`_output_tuple` uses `isinstance(item, OutputDeclaration.__value__)`. This works for a union-typed `type` alias. `require_iterable_of` (`validation.py:75-91`) names the bad index.

findings.title: Error type survives copy and pickle
findings.description: `InvalidParametersError` passes `issues` as its single `args` element, so copy and pickle rebuild it. There is a test for this. The `TYPE_CHECKING` import avoids a runtime cycle with `declarations.py`. No exceptions are swallowed anywhere in the diff. The one `except OverflowError` in `as_real` has a justifying comment.

findings.title: Tests cover the boundaries and enforce structure
findings.description: The tests cover bounds, NaN and infinity, bool rejection, int64 limits, invalid-slot masking, ties and ordering, and non-canonical display hints. The import-boundary tests assert that the new modules define no `CANONICAL_TYPE`. They also keep `display.py` from importing `series` or `declarations`.

findings.title: Minor style points
findings.description: `_require_series` uses `assert isinstance(...)` to narrow the type after `require_instance`. This is acceptable, but `assert` is stripped under `python -O`. It only affects type narrowing, since `require_instance` already raises, so no change is required. The `# pyright: ignore` on the `isinstance` check in `LabelVocabulary.__post_init__` is justified by the comment above it.
